line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Bc5 Nxe5 Bxf2+ Kxf2 Nxe5 d4 Qf6+ Kg1 Ng6 Be3
teaches: A king dragged out by a sacrifice is not in danger once it has a square to tuck into and the checks run out — walk it to safety by hand, then develop the piece that props up the centre, because the attacker who spent material on the exposure has to show a threat before you have finished.
explains: The bishop comes to e3 holding the pawn on d4 and covering the king's corner behind it. The king has stepped off the open file, the checks are finished, and the extra piece is still on the board.
